- issues opened in `story-repo`#5 ("Interim results from experiment-repo for C1–C7 (main G/T/S runs done; extras, synthetic, scope pending)") by `experiment-repo`  > Source: experiment-repo main @ 523326b, files in results/ (mapping in experiment-repo#3). Matrix: 238 models x 328 text tasks, 45,775 cells (59% dense), 83 org groups; held-out: G = 10 group folds (238 models, 83 groups), T = 37 groups (68 models), S = 32 groups (60 models). k grid {1,2,3,5,8,12,20,32,50,80,109}; error in raw points (main_score x 100). These are measurements, not yet all final; what is still running: extra baselines, synthetic ladder, scope sweeps.
  > 
  > **C1 structure (H1).** The rank is not pinned by the data: parallel analysis gives 5 (pairwise) / 8 (EM-completed) / 10 (mean-imputed), inner group-CV picks 16 (curve flattens from rank ~12: standardised RMSE 0.456 @12, 0.448 @16, 0.449 @24), Gavish-Donoho gives 56. The spectrum has one dominant component (63% of variance) and a long tail. Say 'low-rank with an ambiguous tail', not 'rank r'.
  > 
  > **C2 headline curve (G, S6+P5, equal-weight mean of per-model RMSE; group-bootstrap 90% CI).** k=1: 9.50 [8.97,10.09]; k=3: 7.41; k=8: 6.85; k=20: 6.28 [5.94,6.61]; k=50: 5.98; k=109: 5.74. Own all-others floor ~5.3 throughout. Benchmark-mean baseline 15.7, mean-offset (S0+P1) 9.3-12.5 at k=1..20. Excess over floor (S6+P5): 4.2 @k=1, 1.6 @8, 1.08 @20, 0.71 @50, 0.46 @109. So: the error approaches but at the grid's end never reaches the floor.
  > 
  > **C3 k*(eps).** Primary margins delta ~ 0.1 pt are far narrower than anything attainable (G: not reached on the grid, 98% of bootstrap draws never reach it); only the secondary margin delta_floor = 0.25 x mean floor_j ~ 1.2 pt (declared in PREREG Addendum 1 before any contrast) is reachable: empirical k* = 20 [12,32] vs T1-predicted k* = 3 (G, all); on the fixed subset (models with >109 run cells) k* = 50 [20,50]. T split: k* 5 vs predicted 3; S split: 8 vs 5. T1 predicts 5.7 RMSE at k=20 where 6.3 is measured. The theory is optimistic: the gap is the misfit term (Fig. 3), see results/fig3_decomposition.csv: at k=20, measured MSE 44.8 = noise 30.6 + noise misfit 1.0 + design 2.1 + estimation misfit 11.0 (CI 7.9-14.1). Under extrapolation (S, T) the misfit is in the all-others floor itself (floor^2 exceeds the fitted noise by ~60-90 pt^2).
  > 
  > **C4 design vs random (H2), primary contrast S6+P5 vs S0+P5, G.** gain = RMSE(S0)-RMSE(S6) [90% CI]: k=1 1.83 [1.56,2.11]; k=3 1.67; k=8 0.77 [0.66,0.88]; k=20 0.51 [0.34,0.71]; k=32 0.08 [-0.20,0.31]; k=50 0.12; k=109 -0.10 [-0.47,0.26]. Verdict at primary delta: 'design helps' for k<=20, 'undecided' for k>=32 (CI too wide to claim equivalence at +-0.1 pt); at delta_floor: 'design helps' k<=3, 'random matches' k>=8 (k=5 undecided). Same on the fixed subset. T and S: gains larger (S: 4.3 @k=1, 1.8 @k=20) and still positive at k=20-50. The honest sentence: the benefit of design is large for k<=5, is about half a point at k=8-20 and vanishes (within +-1.2 pt) from k~8 on a 1.2-pt scale, not on a 0.1-pt scale.
  > 
  > **Caution for any cross-rule claim.** Raw RMSE across selection rules is confounded by which cells remain as targets at large k: S2 (highest variance) shows RMSE 3.83 at k=109 (below the floor 5.3) only because it reveals the hardest benchmarks and its targets are easy (its own floor is 3.27). Compare rules on excess over the model's own floor on the same targets (columns excess_raw / gain_excess I am adding to curves.csv and contrast file); on that scale S6 is best at every k (G: excess @20 S6 1.08, S5 1.17, S0 1.50, S2 1.75, S4 2.31, S1 2.58) and S1 (popularity) is worst. Figures should plot excess, or both.
  > 
  > **C5 adaptivity (T3).** unit test passes (results/unit_t3.json): with known parameters the posterior covariance does not depend on y, so adaptive = batch; the claim 'adaptivity gives no gain under the model' is a theorem, the empirical adaptive baseline (S7) is still running.
  > 
  > **Not yet available:** Fig.5 scope (training size M, missing rate, logit transform, task-type granularity: running), synthetic ladder and estimation-term-vs-M (running), P2-P6 inference baselines and S3/S7/S6u (running
